queue.title: Exploration: loops as an agent-usable tool (supersedes Proposal A)
queue.why: The operator rejected Proposal A from 2026-08-17-architecture-proposals.md on its merits during prep. This exploration must say so explicitly and record why, so Proposal A is not re-proposed later.
must_cover: WHY Loop.charter_id is rejected: hub/hub/api/v1/agents.py:1060-1064 builds the turn's charter from agent_row.charter_id. A loop already has an agent, and that agent already has a charter. A second charter would compete for the same turn with no precedence rule. Operator's own words: 'A loop or a job has an agent attached to it. This agent has a charter already... So I don't know if a loop earns it's place on agentweave.'

What a Loop DOES legitimately contain, field by field, vs AIJob + Agent: purpose (no -- duplicates AIJob.name/message and the charter), stop_at / stop_when_queue_empties / stop_reason / stopped_at (YES -- a job runs forever, a loop terminates and records why), Task.loop_id (YES -- a scoped backlog). Conclusion to defend: a loop is not 'an agent on a schedule' (a bare AIJob is already exactly that) -- it is a job that ENDS and OWNS A BACKLOG.

The MCP gap: hub/hub/mcp_server.py:503-529 create_job takes only name, agent, message, cron, session_mode. hub/hub/api/v1/jobs.py:93 _loop_opts_in(purpose, stop_at, stop_when_queue_empties) is 'design D6's at least one field rule' -- supply any one to POST /jobs and the job becomes a Loop. So an agent can create a job that runs forever and CANNOT create a loop that ends. Decide: widen create_job, or add a distinct create_loop tool? Argue it, do not assume.
The permission gate already exists: hub/hub/api/v1/jobs.py:21 _require_agent_job_allowance. Confirm agent-created loops inherit it and that no new permission concept is needed -- or say why one is.

The briefing / amnesia problem. hub/hub/scheduler.py:296 _do_fire_job replays job.message verbatim every firing. The agent gets NO queue state -- what is left, what is done, what prior firings concluded. A loop has its own thread (Conversation origin='job', JobRun.conversation_id) but no memory of its own progress. Design the briefing: what goes in, how it is capped so a long-running loop does not dominate its own turn, and where it is assembled (mirror how agents.py:1316 appends the charter to canonical context).

The dangling-agent defect: AIJob.agent is a bare String(64), not an FK to agents.id. hub/hub/scheduler.py:51-56 _job_agent_skip_reason returns None when NO agent row matches the name -- and None means PROCEED. Rename or archive an agent and its loops keep firing at a name nobody owns. Decide whether this change fixes it (refuse to fire + record stop_reason is the obvious shape) or merely records it.

Loops on the roster: the operator's objection implies a loop belongs UNDER its agent, not beside it -- an agent row reading '2 loops, next fires 14:00' rather than claude-dev and nightly-scan as siblings. Take a position.

Forward note, do not build: this is what makes Proposal C (the autonomous session itself as a Loop) reachable, because the missing piece there was always 'how does a firing know where the last one got to' -- which is exactly the briefing.
